attackPath: Concurrent generic PUT/parity api-save requests observe the same version then independently overwrite admin key/permission metadata.
rootCause: Handler version checks preceded unconditional writes; parity updates did not reject a supplied stale version.
impact: Lost credential/permission edits and stale state replacement. No actual historical attacker access asserted.
repair: A dedicated atomic findOneAndUpdate compares id and observed version in the Mongo write; memory equivalent checks/mutates without yielding. Both handlers return 409 for a failed compare. Parity also rejects a supplied stale version.

evidence.layer: Controlled direct handler with explicitly unconfigured in-memory Mongo
evidence.result: Exit 0; each race one HTTP 200 and nineteen 409 responses; winner retained and key unchanged
evidence.compatibility: Three admin response/error regressions rerun and exit 0

mongo.layer: Actual temporary loopback-only single-member Mongo replica set, synthetic direct handler requests and persisted database readback
mongo.result: Exit 0 PASS; generic/parity/mixed each one success and nineteen conflicts; stored key retained; stale supplied editor version rejected; missing-version legacy transition succeeds once; daemon/files removed

remainingLimitations: No configured Atlas, browser, hosted or role authorization proof
Metadata update and separate generic audit insert are not crash atomic
Absent client version cannot prove a stale editor snapshot; server compare still prevents competing observed-version writes
Credential activation, provider rotation and job drain not established
Single local replica member does not prove multi-node failover, load/soak, hosted proxy or configured Atlas behavior
